q-84826.name: Question 1
q-84826.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(-3,-2)$ and which passes through the point $(2,3)?$
q-84826.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-3,-2),$ and so we have

$$
x+3=2pt,\,y+2=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(2,3),$ we can substitute $x=2$ and $y=3$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5=2pt \\ 5=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =2pt \\ t & =\frac{5}{2p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =p{(\frac{5}{2p})}^{2} \\ 5 & =p\cdot \frac{25}{4{p}^{2}} \\ 5 & =\frac{25}{4p} \\ p & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+3=2(\frac{5}{4})t,\,y+2=(\frac{5}{4}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+3=\frac{5}{2}t,\,y+2=\frac{5}{4}{t}^{2}.
$$

q-106451.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(3,-2),$ and passes through the point $(7,-6).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(3,-2),$ and so we have

$$
x-3=2pt,\,y+2=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(7,-6),$ we can substitute $x=7$ and $y=-6$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4=2pt \\ -4=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ -4 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ -4 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-3=2(-1)t,\,y+2=(-1){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$

q-106455.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(3,3)$ and which passes through the point $(7,5)?$
q-106455.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(3,3),$ and so we have

$$
x-3=2pt,\,y-3=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(7,5),$ we can substitute $x=7$ and $y=5$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4=2pt \\ 2=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ 2 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ 1 & =\frac{2}{p} \\ p & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-3=2(2)t,\,y-3=(2){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-3=4t,\,y-3=2{t}^{2}.
$$

q-106447.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(-1,2),$ and passes through the point $(1,4).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-1,2),$ and so we have

$$
x+1=2pt,\,y-2=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(1,4),$ we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=4$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2=2pt \\ 2=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2pt \\ 1 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =p{(\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ 2 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ 2 & =\frac{1}{p} \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+1=2(\frac{1}{2})t,\,y-2=(\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+1=t,\,y-2=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}.
$$

q-84819.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(2,-2),$ and passes through the point $(4,2).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(2,-2),$ and so we have

$$
x-2=2pt,\,y+2=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(4,2),$ we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=2$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2=2pt \\ 4=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2pt \\ 1 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =p{(\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ 4 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{p} \\ p & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-2=2(\frac{1}{4})t,\,y+2=(\frac{1}{4}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-2=\frac{1}{2}t,\,y+2=\frac{1}{4}{t}^{2}.
$$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(2,2),$ and so we have

$$
x-2=p{t}^{2},\,y-2=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(4,6),$ we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=6$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2=p{t}^{2} \\ 4=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ 2 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ 2 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =2.\end{aligned}

$$
x-2=(2){t}^{2},\,y-2=2(2)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-2=2{t}^{2},\,y-2=4t.
$$

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the parabola shown above?

a
x+4=2t,y+4=t2
b
x−4=t2,y−4=2t
c
x−4=2t,y−4=t2
d
x+4=t2,y+4=2t
e
x−4=2t2,y−4=4t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at (4,4), and passes through the point (8,8).

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at (h,k) are

x−h=pt2,y−k=2pt,

where p is constant.

In our case, (h,k)=(4,4), and so we have

x−4=pt2,y−4=2pt.

Since the parabola passes through (8,8), we can substitute x=8 and y=8 into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

{4=pt24=2pt.

Solving the second equation for t, we have

4=2pt2=ptt=2p.

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for p, we get

4=p(2p)24=p⋅4p24=4pp=44p=1.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x−4=(1)t2,y−4=2(1)t,

which simplify to

x−4=t2,y−4=2t.

q-84844.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation $(y-3)^{2}=-12(x-5)?$
q-84844.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h)$ that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),$ we see that the parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(5,3).$ So we have

$$
x-5=p{t}^{2},\,y-3=2pt.
$$

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4p(x-h) & =-12(x-5) \\ 4p(x-5) & =-12(x-5) \\ 4p & =-12 \\ p & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-5=(-3){t}^{2},\,y-3=2(-3)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-5=-3{t}^{2},\,y-3=-6t.
$$

Question 9
?

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation (y−3)2=−12(x−5)?

a
x+5=−t2,y+3=6t
b
x+5=−4t2,y+3=12t
c
x−5=−3t2,y−3=3t
d
x−5=−3t2,y−3=−6t
e
x−5=3t2,y−3=−12t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola (y−k)2=4p(x−h) that has its vertex at (h,k) are

x−h=pt2,y−k=2pt,

where p is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case (y−k)2=4p(x−h), we see that the parabola has its vertex at (h,k)=(5,3). So we have

x−5=pt2,y−3=2pt.

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for p, we get

4p(x−h)=−12(x−5)4p(x−5)=−12(x−5)4p=−12p=−3.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x−5=(−3)t2,y−3=2(−3)t,

which simplify to

x−5=−3t2,y−3=−6t.

q-84846.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation $(y+2)^{2}=\frac{1}{2}(x+5)?$
q-84846.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h)$ that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),$ we see that the parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-5,-2).$ So we have

$$
x+5=p{t}^{2},\,y+2=2pt.
$$

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4p(x-h) & =\frac{1}{2}(x+5) \\ 4p(x+5) & =\frac{1}{2}(x+5) \\ 4p & =\frac{1}{2} \\ p & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+5=(\frac{1}{8}){t}^{2},\,y+2=2(\frac{1}{8})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+5=\frac{1}{8}{t}^{2},\,y+2=\frac{1}{4}t.
$$

q-84846.html:
Question 10
?

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation (y+2)2=12(x+5)?

a
x+5=12t2,y+2=t
b
x−5=14t2,y−2=18t
c
x+5=t2,y+2=2t
d
x+5=18t2,y+2=14t
e
x−5=2t2,y−2=t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola (y−k)2=4p(x−h) that has its vertex at (h,k) are

x−h=pt2,y−k=2pt,

where p is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case (y−k)2=4p(x−h), we see that the parabola has its vertex at (h,k)=(−5,−2). So we have

x+5=pt2,y+2=2pt.

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for p, we get

4p(x−h)=12(x+5)4p(x+5)=12(x+5)4p=12p=18.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x+5=(18)t2,y+2=2(18)t,

which simplify to

x+5=18t2,y+2=14t.

q-106506.name: Question 11
q-106506.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x+1=2{t}^{2},\,y+3=4t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
q-106506.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{x+1}{2},\,t=\frac{y+3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{y+3}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{x+1}{2}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{16} & =\frac{x+1}{2} \\ (y+3)^{2} & =16\cdot (\frac{x+1}{2}) \\ (y+3)^{2} & =8(x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

q-106506.html:
Question 11
?

Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

x+1=2t2,y+3=4t,t∈(−∞,∞).

a
(y+3)2=8(x+1)
b
(y+3)2=−8(x+1)
c
(x+1)2=4(y+3)
d
(x+1)2=8(y+3)
e
(y+3)2=4(x+1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's make t the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

t2=x+12,t=y+34.

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

t2=(y+34)2=(y+3)216.

We can now eliminate the parameter t by substituting the above into the equation t2=x+12 and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

(y+3)216=x+12(y+3)2=16⋅(x+12)(y+3)2=8(x+1).

q-106502.name: Question 12
q-106502.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x-2=-4t,\,y-5=-2{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
q-106502.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =-\frac{x-2}{4},\,{t}^{2}=-\frac{y-5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(-\frac{x-2}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-\frac{y-5}{2}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16} & =-\frac{y-5}{2} \\ (x-2)^{2} & =-8(y-5).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12

Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

x−2=−4t,y−5=−2t2,t∈(−∞,∞).

a
(y−5)2=−8(x−2)
b
(x−5)2=−8(y−2)
c
(x−2)2=−8(y−5)
d
(x−2)2=8(y−5)
e
(y−5)2=8(x−2)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's make t the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

t=−x−24,t2=−y−52.

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

t2=(−x−24)2=(x−2)216.

We can now eliminate the parameter t by substituting the above into the equation t2=−y−52 and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

(x−2)216=−y−52(x−2)2=−8(y−5).

q-84849.name: Question 13
q-84849.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x-4=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2},\,y+1=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
q-84849.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =2(x-4),\,t=y+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =(y+1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=2(x-4)$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =2(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

q-84859.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x+1=-\frac{5}{4}{t}^{2},\,y-1=-\frac{5}{2}t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
q-84859.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-\frac{4(x+1)}{5},\,t=-\frac{2(y-1)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(-\frac{2(y-1)}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4(y-1)^{2}}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-\frac{4(x+1)}{5}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4(y-1)^{2}}{25} & =-\frac{4(x+1)}{5} \\ (y-1)^{2} & =\frac{25}{4}\cdot (-\frac{4(x+1)}{5}) \\ (y-1)^{2} & =-5(x+1).\end{aligned}
$$
